prompt: Design a team project management tool — a workspace dashboard showing active projects, team workload, upcoming deadlines, and recent activity, and a project detail page with tasks, progress, assignees, and timeline. Make it feel clean, productive, and professional.
title: Team Project Workspace

issues.description: The workload overview only renders DATA.people.slice(0, 4), although the brief requires a compact comparison across the 5–15 person team. It also shows only percentages and names; it does not show assigned task counts, capacity indicators, or explicit labels such as On track, Near capacity, and Over capacity. This omits a critical home workflow and relies on a visual bar/color treatment rather than clear status text.

WorkloadOverview calls Avatar with src={person.avatar}, alt={person.name}, and size="sm", but Avatar expects name, initials, and a numeric size. The supplied people data has initials but no avatar field, so the rendered workload identities have no initials and the inline width/height receive the invalid string value "sm". This can produce missing or malformed team identity content.

ProjectRow is implemented as an individual Card, indicating a stack of generic bordered cards for the active project list. The brief explicitly calls for active project rows rather than a card grid, and the universal surface guide prefers divided data rows for dense operational lists.

The deterministic V17 gate reports approximately 60% empty viewport, approximately 40% content fill, and missing supporting context on the home screen. This is below the required feed density and indicates that active projects, upcoming deadlines, and recent activity are not sufficiently visible around the dominant workload moment.

The deterministic V17 gate reports only 2 modules on the detail screen, approximately 20% content fill, and missing supporting context, while this screen requires a focused project pane, milestone timeline, scoped task list, and a clear add or assign work action. The rendered detail view is therefore materially too sparse for the required project workflow.

The screen defines WorkloadOverview and ProjectRow inline instead of using shared components under src/components/. The V17 gate reports 0 custom components rendered despite the screen needing a product-specific workload or project component, so the current implementation fails both the shared-component standard and the required authored product structure.

MilestoneTimeline and TaskRow are defined inline in the screen rather than as shared product components. The V17 gate reports 0 custom components for detail, which contributes to the screen reading as generic primitives rather than a focused project-management workspace.

The geometry measurements report that the Sora font is not loaded on both verified screens. Since Sora is the specified display font, the current typography cannot meet the Apple design-language type direction. The measurements also report 4 off-grid elements on home and 2 on detail.

The screenshot contains an extremely large blank vertical region above the project header, far beyond the 32–64px rhythm required by the layout law. It delays the primary project workflow and makes the desktop app feel visually broken rather than spacious.

The dashboard has the same oversized empty region above the actual content. This is not intentional whitespace because it contains no product content and pushes the workload hero far below the initial viewport.

The project summary does not visibly show the project owner name or a numeric progress percentage. The summary labels are also mismatched: OWNER is followed by '18 of 25 tasks' and PROGRESS is followed by '4 days remaining'. The detail intent requires project name, owner, status, and progress.

The Active Tasks rows visibly show task title, priority, due date, and dependency text, but no assignee and no clear task status beyond generic check icons. The brief requires status, assignee, priority, due date, and dependency indicators in the scoped task list.

The Project Timeline is very vertically stretched, with large gaps between milestones and little supporting information such as planned dates, current phase context, or overdue/blocked work. The timeline reads as sparse rather than as a useful project progress view.

The Team workload panel shows only four people and only percentage bars. It omits assigned task counts and explicit workload states such as On track, Near capacity, and Over capacity, which are critical requirements and cannot be inferred from color or percentage alone.

Active project rows show project name, owner, a status badge, date, and progress, but do not visibly show task completion or next milestone. These are required fields for the active projects dashboard.
Upcoming deadlines list only project names and dates. The required responsible person and days remaining are absent, so the section does not support the intended deadline triage workflow.
Recent activity entries include action descriptions and relative timestamps but do not identify the actor. Meaningful activity must include actor names along with the action and timestamp.

The Team workload panel is stretched into a large bordered surface with member names at the far left and bars at the far right, leaving excessive unused space between each row. A compact comparison table or divided row layout would better match the desktop operations dashboard intent.

The detail page uses multiple bordered card treatments, including the task list and Project Insights tiles, while the primary project facts and timeline are mostly plain. The hierarchy would be clearer with a restrained summary band and divided data rows rather than several similarly weighted bordered surfaces.

reviewResult.summary: The screens compile and use the correct desktop sidebar/topbar product shell, but both views are substantially underfilled and omit critical operational content. Home does not provide the required full-team workload comparison, and the malformed Avatar props prevent team identities from rendering correctly. Detail is too sparse to support a focused project workflow. The implementation also relies on inline generic blocks, has individual card treatment for dense project rows, and does not load the specified Sora font.
requiredFixes: Update src/screens/home.jsx so the workload overview compares all 8 team members and shows assigned task counts, capacity indicators, and explicit text statuses such as On track, Near capacity, and Over capacity.
Fix the Avatar usage in src/screens/home.jsx: pass name, initials, and a numeric size to Avatar instead of src, alt, and size="sm", so team identities render visibly and accessibly.
Increase meaningful content density in src/screens/home.jsx by rendering the active project rows, upcoming deadlines, recent activity, and supporting workload context in the primary viewport.

Complete src/screens/detail.jsx with the project facts, milestone timeline, scoped task list, dependency information, and the add or assign work action so the detail screen has at least three meaningful modules.
Extract WorkloadOverview, ProjectRow, MilestoneTimeline, and TaskRow into shared files under src/components/ and ensure at least one product-specific component is visibly rendered on each screen.
Load the Sora display font in the application theme and correct the measured off-grid elements in src/screens/home.jsx and src/screens/detail.jsx.
detail: Remove the enormous empty region above the project header and bring the focused project workspace into the initial viewport.

detail: Correct the project summary labels and values: show the actual owner name, explicit status, and a visible 72% progress value rather than placing task counts under OWNER and days remaining under PROGRESS.
detail: Expand each task row to visibly include status, assignee, priority, due date, and dependency indicators as required by the project task workflow.
home: Remove the enormous empty region above the dashboard content and establish the workload summary as the first visible product moment.

home: Make the workload comparison complete: include assigned task counts, capacity indicators, and explicit On track, Near capacity, or Over capacity labels for a 5–15 person team. Do not communicate workload status through percentages or color alone.
home: Enrich active project rows with task completion, current status, owner, progress percentage, and next milestone; the current rows show only a small subset of the required project data.
home: Add responsible person and days remaining to each upcoming deadline item, and add actor names to recent activity entries.
home: Reduce the excessive empty space inside the Team workload panel and align the member data into a compact comparison layout.
